'''Keita Bates-Diop''' (born January 23, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]].

==High school career==
The [[small forward]] played for [[University High School (Normal, Illinois)|University High School]] in [[Normal, Illinois]].  He averaged 18.4 points, 6.7 rebounds and 2.3 blocks as a junior. He was considered one of the top 5 candidates for Illinois Mr. Basketball by the [[Chicago Tribune]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-11-27/sports/ct-spt-1128-prep-bkb-season-pvw-top-5-mr-basketbal-20131127_1_tyler-ulis-stevenson-brunson-boys-hoops|title=Boys hoops - Top 5 Mr. Basketball candidates|accessdate=January 31, 2014|date=November 27, 2013|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}}</ref> Bates-Diop was ranked no. 24 nationally in his class by [[Rivals.com]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2014/03/nik_stauskas_a_second-team_all.html|title=Michigan's Nik Stauskas gets All-America honor; recruit Kameron Chatman a prep All-American|accessdate=March 12, 2014|date=March 10, 2014|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Baumgardner, Nick}}</ref>

==College career==
Bates-Diop was a bench player as a freshman at OSU in the 2014-15 season. As a sophomore, he expanded his role on the team and averaged 11.8 points and 6.4 rebounds per game.<ref name=markus/> But as a junior, he suffered a stress fracture in his left leg, sitting out all but the first nine games, while the Buckeyes limped to a 17-15 record without him. In those nine games, Bates-Diop averaged 9.7 points and 5.2 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Birdsong|first1=Nick|title=Ohio State's Keita Bates-Diop is the difference maker the Buckeyes needed all along|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/ohio-state-buckeyes-basketball-schedule-roster-keita-bates-diop-2018-mock-draft-analysis/ro4ahghrqvq01scjf6x4zulkl|accessdate=January 19, 2018|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=November 22, 2017}}</ref> He was granted a medical redshirt and came into his redshirt junior campaign one of the top options for new coach [[Chris Holtmann]].<ref name=markus>{{cite news|last1=Markus|first1=Don|title=In order to beat Ohio State, Maryland has to stop Keita Bates-Diop|url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/tracking-the-terps/bs-sp-maryland-ohio-state-bates-diop-0111-story.html|accessdate=January 19, 2018|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|date=January 11, 2018}}</ref>

Bates-Diop earned his first Big Ten player of the week honors on December 11, 2017, after notching a career-high 27 points in a   97-62 win over [[William & Mary Tribe men's basketball|William & Mary]].<ref name=MSOSEWMBY>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/121117aac.html|title=Michigan State, Ohio State Earn Weekly Men’s Basketball Honors: Buckeyes’ Keita Bates-Diop earns Player of the Week award; Spartans’ Jaren Jackson Jr. named Freshman of the Week|accessdate=December 11, 2017|date=December 11, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=BigTen.org}}</ref> On January 9, 2018, Bates-Diop was recognized as the Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] after strong performances against [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball]] and [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]]. Bates-Diop tied a then-career high with 27 points and grabbed 13 rebounds in a victory against Iowa. Against top-ranked Michigan State, he scored a career-high 32 points in a 80-64 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2018/oscar180109.html|title=Ohio State's Bates-Diop Is Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week|accessdate=January 19, 2018|date=January 9, 2018|publisher=The [[United States Basketball Writers Association]]}}</ref> He also received his second Big Ten player of the week recognition.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/010818aag.html|title=Maryland, Ohio State Earn Weekly Men’s Basketball Honors: Buckeyes’ Keita Bates-Diop earns Player of the Week award; Terrapins’ Bruno Fernando named Freshman of the Week|website=www.bigten.org|language=en|accessdate=January 8, 2018|date=January 8, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}}</ref> Bates-Diop received his second consecutive player of the week nod on January 15, with a 26 point, eight rebound outing in a 91-69 win over [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] and 20 points, nine rebounds in a victory versus [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/011518aad.html|title=Michigan State, Ohio State Earn Weekly Men’s Basketball Honors: Buckeyes’ Keita Bates-Diop earns second-consecutive Player of the Week award; Spartans’ Jaren Jackson Jr. named Freshman of the Week for third time|website=www.bigten.org|language=en|accessdate=January 15, 2018|date=January 15, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}}</ref>

On February 26, 2018, Bates-Diop was named the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022618aad.html |title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN |date=February 26, 2018 |accessdate=February 26, 2018}}</ref> He averaged 19.8 points and 8.7 rebounds per game. Following Ohio State's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]], Bates-Diop announced his intention to forgo his final season of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA Draft]], where he is expected to be a first round selection.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Adrian |last=Wojnarowski|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22916723/ohio-state-buckeyes-forward-keita-bates-diop-enter-nba-draft|title=Buckeyes forward Keita Bates-Diop to enter NBA draft|work=[[ESPN]]|access-date= March 26, 2018|date=March 26, 2018}}</ref>
